entries.removal_criteria: Registered budget-effect targets receive a dedicated target-migration packet and source, runtime-string, wheel, documentation, effect-registry, monkeypatch, and pickle audits show no remaining compatibility caller.

Source, runtime-string, wheel, documentation, effect-registry, monkeypatch, and pickle audits show no remaining implementation caller after one supported compatibility release.

The two measured flat-path callers are repointed at the owner -- daedalus/interfaces/http/read.py (deferred import in the GET /api/catalogue branch) and tools/smoke_packaged_resources.py (wheel smoke check, which must keep exercising the packaged path it actually ships) -- and source, runtime-string, wheel, documentation, effect-registry, monkeypatch, and pickle audits show no remaining caller. The wheel audit is not optional here: the smoke check imports this name out of an installed site-packages tree, so a green source audit alone would not prove the flat name is unused.
The Ikarus orchestration package owns the public name and all scheduler callers have migrated without changing serialized identities.

MEASURED at creation (G1-FLAT-01): this facade has ZERO callers -- its only importer was tests/test_ikarus_runtime_events.py, which G1-FLAT-01 repointed at the owner because it reads the implementation source. It is retained only because the flat path is named by .github/workflows/g1-ikarus-runtime-events.yml and docs/research/hermes-agent-v2026.8.19-provenance.json, and because the module is a deliberately unwired seam (docs/work-packets/G1-IKARUS-03) whose future consumer has not landed. Delete it in the packet that lands that consumer against daedalus.orchestration.ikarus_runtime_events, or sooner if the owner decides the flat name was never public. A shim with no caller is debt, and this row exists so it is counted as debt rather than mistaken for compatibility.
A dedicated packet proves old imports and pickle names absent, preserves registry identity, and replaces the retained source without weakening owner approval.
All callers use responsibility modules and a clean wheel import audit observes no facade imports.

Source, runtime-string, wheel, documentation, effect-registry, and pickle audits show no callers of the lane, worktree, or chip-publication compatibility facades; the registered effect targets and anchors remain unchanged.

The three measured flat-path callers are repointed at the owner -- daedalus/runbook.py (deferred, inside the engine == 'langgraph' branch; the deferral is optional-dependency isolation and must survive the repoint), experiments/opus_fleet_watchdog/core.py, and tests/test_opus_fleet_watchdog.py -- CLAUDE.md's reference to daedalus/langgraph_adapter.py is updated to the owner path, and source, runtime-string, wheel, documentation, and pickle audits show no remaining caller. Removal must not convert any deferred langgraph import to module scope: tests/test_langgraph_adapter.py::test_nothing_imports_langgraph_at_module_scope pins that the package still imports with the orchestration extra absent.
